subject: Decision Making
title: When Nudges Backfire
description: A 60-second lesson on When Nudges Backfire.

hook.text: A daycare fined parents for late pickup. Late pickups increased.

buildup.text: Economists Uri Gneezy and Aldo Rustichini documented this. The fine replaced guilt with a price.

discovery.text: Nudges backfire when they crowd out intrinsic motivation. Financial incentives can destroy moral reasons that worked.

twist.text: Removing the fine did not restore the old behavior. Once the social norm broke, it stayed broken.

climax.text: Not all nudges work and some cause lasting damage. Testing on small groups before scaling is essential to avoid.

punchline.text: Fine for lateness? More lateness. Some nudges destroy the norms they need.

quiz.question: Why did fining late parents backfire?
options: The fine replaced moral guilt with a price, turning lateness into a paid service
